archetype.name: Pocket Passer (short-area mode)
archetype.definition: An 18-year veteran working almost entirely from the pocket. In 2026 he wins with timing throws underneath and in the 10-19 yard window, and he barely runs or scrambles at all.

report.headline: Still a sharp intermediate passer, but the deep ball has vanished
report.take:
Stafford arrives at 38.8 off a 2025 that ranked first in passing yards and touchdowns, with an 0.228 EPA per play. This year he is a different, smaller version of that player. His EPA per dropback of 0.09 ranks 20th of 49. His yards per attempt are down 1.02 from last season, his aggressiveness has dropped 5.7 points to 13.58%, and his intended air yards sit at 7.63. Counting volume still looks good, 4th in passing yards and on pace for 4,484, because the Rams pass more than situation predicts (+3.4, 4th). The per-play quality is closer to league-average starter than MVP candidate.

The split that explains the season is depth. Between 10 and 19 air yards he is still very good: 0.373 EPA per attempt, the single biggest source of his value. Past 20 yards it has collapsed. He completes 24.2% of those throws, 13.2 points under expectation, with three interceptions on 33 attempts. The offense has responded by shrinking the field. In Weeks 6 through 8 his intended air yards were 4.8, 4.9 and 4.3. Last season's 19.3% aggressiveness was actually the outlier. His earlier Rams years ran in the 12-13% range, so the caution itself is not alarming. The deep inaccuracy when he does let it go is what is new.

The 3-0 run over the last three weeks flatters him. In that stretch his EPA per dropback fell to 0.028, his yards per attempt to 5.98 and his CPOE to -1.9. His passing EPA averaged 0.9 a game against a season average of 3.6. The wins came largely from a defense that ranks 4th in EPA and 2nd against deep passes, which lets McVay play a field-position game. Third downs are a real problem: -0.293 EPA per play and a 37% conversion rate at an average of 7.3 yards to go. Those numbers point to an offense that is fine on early downs and stalls when it has to throw into longer distances.

The structural positives are real and should last. He rarely takes sacks: a 3.6% sack rate, 5th best, with pressure-to-sack among the better marks and improving for three straight seasons. He is efficient under center (0.165 EPA) and in no-huddle (0.396). The interceptions are the other constant: 9 of them, ranked 45th, which fits a career of high pick counts. Nacua is doubtful with a knee injury, and that is the immediate swing. Adams has been the more efficient target per throw. Without Nacua's 93 targets, though, more of the volume goes to Higbee and Kyren Williams, whose targets have produced little.

strengths.title: Intermediate window still produces
strengths.body: His 10-19 yard throws carry 0.373 EPA per attempt, the largest share of his passing value. This is timing and anticipation into zone voids, the skill that made his 2025 season. It isn't built on a fluky handful of plays: it has held up over 79 attempts.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks and negative plays
strengths.body: His 3.6% sack rate ranks 5th, and his pressure-to-sack rate of 24% ranks 12th. He gets the ball out or throws it away rather than eating losses. His career pressure-to-sack has fallen steadily since 2023, so this is a skill, not a blocking illusion. That matters with a starting guard banged up.

strengths.title: Red zone and tempo efficiency
strengths.body: Fourteen of his 16 touchdowns have come in the red zone, at 0.251 EPA per play, and he is +2.5 CPOE there. In no-huddle he has posted 0.396 EPA with a 68.5% success rate, which suggests he is at his best when he controls the pace. The no-huddle sample is 54 plays, so it is a hint more than a fact.

concerns.title: Deep accuracy has fallen apart
concerns.body: On throws of 20+ air yards he is completing 24.2% of passes, 13.2 points under expected, with three interceptions on 33 attempts. The scheme has pulled back on shots in response. That is why his yards per attempt sits a full yard under last season even with completion percentage up. At his age this could be a physical decline rather than noise, but the sample is small enough that a couple of hits would move it.

concerns.title: Efficiency sagging despite the wins
concerns.body: Over the last three games his EPA per dropback is 0.028, and his YPA and CPOE are both well below his season marks. The 3-0 record reflects a top-five defense, not his play. Third downs (-0.293 EPA, four interceptions) are where the drives die.

concerns.title: Interceptions remain a tax
concerns.body: Nine picks rank 45th of 49. Seven of them came on throws of 10+ air yards. This is a lifelong trait rather than a new flaw: his career is full of high interception ranks. Expect roughly one a game to continue.

trend.note: Big outings in Weeks 2 and 5 carried the early numbers. Since Week 6 the passing tree has shrunk and per-play efficiency has slid, even as the Rams won three straight on defense.

nextGame.headline: Worst pass defense in the league, but a lopsided script
nextGame.body:
By EPA, Arizona's pass defense ranks 32nd, its defense against short throws ranks 29th, and it allows 2.44 passing touchdowns a game to quarterbacks (30th). That lines up neatly with a passer now living underneath and in the intermediate range. The caution is Week 6. Against this same defense, as a 12.5-point favorite, he threw at 4.8 intended air yards, was pressured on 25% of dropbacks, took three sacks and finished at -2.6 EPA in a loss. A soft matchup is not automatic production for this version of the offense.

Availability tilts the script. Puka Nacua is doubtful with a knee injury, which pushes Davante Adams into the lead role. Adams has been the more efficient target per throw, but depth behind him at tight end is thin with Ferguson on IR. Steve Avila is questionable, and IR remains possible, so the interior pass protection could be weakened. Arizona is worse off: Minshew is doubtful with a likely torn UCL, Michael Wilson is out for the season, and its running back room is gutted. A 9.5-point spread and a 40.5 total point to the Rams leading early and leaning on the run. That favors efficiency over volume for Stafford.

keyMatchups.title: Adams against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Arizona allows 0.51 EPA per target to opposing WR1s, 29th, even though those receivers' fantasy totals have come in under their averages. With Nacua likely out, Adams becomes the primary read. His 0.451 EPA per target is the best of Stafford's receivers.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into a soft underneath zone
keyMatchups.body: Arizona's 29th-ranked defense against short passes plays straight into Stafford's under-10 attempts, where he completes 77% of throws. If the Rams stay under center and use play-action, where he has been far better than from shotgun, the efficiency should be there.

keyMatchups.title: Script and total cap volume
keyMatchups.body: A low 40.5 total against a Cardinals offense likely missing its quarterback and top receiver points to a Rams lead and plenty of runs late. His leading-by-9+ EPA has been strong, but the attempts thin out in those spots.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Rams take any 20+ yard shots against the league's most generous pass defense, or keep the field compressed as they did in Week 6.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is sustainable because the Rams keep passing above expectation. Expect roughly 215-265 yards a game, enough to stay top-10 in total yards. The efficiency is closer to the 0.09 EPA-per-dropback passer of this season than the 2025 version, unless the deep ball returns. The intermediate game and sack avoidance are durable and should keep the floor stable. The red-zone touchdown rate should hold reasonably well given his career, while the near-one-interception-a-game rate is simply who he is.

The biggest variable is Nacua's knee. Without him the target pool tilts toward Higbee and Kyren Williams, whose targets have added little or negative EPA, and pressure lands on Adams to carry the efficiency. A strong defense also means fewer shootouts, which caps ceilings.
swingFactors: Nacua's knee and how long he misses
Whether the deep ball comes back or stays shelved

confidence.note: Nine starts and a stable role, but the Nacua injury and a small deep-ball sample add real uncertainty.
